findings.title: Materials' 66-point lens gap signals collapse
findings.body: Materials' forward P/E sits at the 15th percentile while its trailing multiple is at the 81st, a 66-point divergence that dwarfs every other sector. The market is underwriting 115 percent earnings growth, a bet that current margins are a trough and will reverse violently.

findings.title: Information Technology's cheapness is an earnings bet
findings.body: Information Technology's forward multiple is at the 19th percentile, yet its trailing P/E stands at the 58th. The 38-point gap implies 66 percent earnings growth, meaning the market is paying up for a recovery that has not shown up in reported results.

findings.title: Real Estate's forward premium masks a decline
findings.body: Real Estate's forward P/E of 33.55 is at the 6th percentile, but it is still richer than its trailing multiple, which sits at the 18th percentile. The market is pricing a 4 percent earnings decline, yet the forward lens is not cheaper—an unusual combination that suggests the sector's cheapness is relative to its own history, not to its earnings trajectory.
